READY
The buggy method is `org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.contains(char)`.

Diagnosis:
- `StrBuilder` uses `size` as the logical string length and `buffer` as a larger backing array.
- After `deleteFirst("three")`, `deleteImpl(...)` reduces `size` but does not clear stale trailing characters from `buffer`.
- `contains(char)` incorrectly loops over `thisBuf.length` instead of `size`:

```java
for (int i = 0; i < thisBuf.length; i++) {
```

- So it searches beyond the logical end of the string and can find deleted characters still present in unused buffer slots.

Why this matches the failure:
- After deleting `"three"` from `"onetwothree"`, the logical content is `"onetwo"` with `size == 6`.
- Dynamic verification confirmed `buffer.length == 43`, and `contains('h')` returned true only after the loop advanced to an index beyond `size`.
- That exactly explains the failing assertion: `contains(char)` is “looking beyond the end of the string”.

The fix should make `contains(char)` iterate only up to `size`, not the full backing array length.
